sources.citation: OLAC: 'OLAC resources in and about the Mulgi language' [mvh], static catalogue page up to date as of 2024-12-07 (Wayback), plus 2026 OLAC search-index query.
sources.note: Catalogue lists only Glottolog, Ethnologue, an SIL Tchad literacy primer (Gustafsson ed. 2020, oai:sil.org:83684) and two 2020 SIL Tchad Corona videos; no language description of any kind.

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2025. Palatalization and labialization in the Chadic languages of Chad. Afrika und Übersee 98: 41-62. DOI 10.15460/auue.2025.98.1.392
sources.note: Covers Heɗe, Somrai, Gabri, Kabalay, Mawa; Mulgi/Mire not mentioned; nothing on stress for Mire.

sources.citation: Roberts, James. 2021. Initial findings on the Boor language. Afrika und Übersee 94: 127-140. DOI 10.15460/auue.2021.94.1.242
sources.note: Only Mire-relevant line (p.131): 'This is reminiscent of the situation in Mulgi (personal field notes), where the phoneme /l/ has allophone [ɽ] before the front vowel /i/.' Confirms unpublished SIL field notes on Mulgi exist; nothing on Mulgi stress or tone.

sources.citation: Jungraithmayr, Herrmann & Carsten Peust. 2019. Notes on Gàlì (Miltu), a moribund Chadic language (Republic of Chad). Folia Orientalia 56: 219-230. DOI 10.24425/for.2019.130711
sources.note: About neighbouring Gali/Miltu only (sec. 2.1.3 Tone: three levels + two contours, 'a tone language'); no Mire data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Peust, Carsten. 2018. The subgrouping of East Chadic. Folia Orientalia 55: 235-253. DOI 10.24425/for.2018.124686
sources.note: Nothing; Mire is not among the 16 East Chadic languages sampled (only documented languages included); no Mire data at all.

sources.citation: Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2016. Ethnologue, 19th ed.: Mulgi [mvh] (Wayback capture 2016-08-13).
sources.note: Nothing; alt. name Mire; Tandjilé Est between Ndam and Kimré; 65% lexical similarity with Ndam, 32% with Kimré; EGIDS 6a.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2011. Change Request Number 2011-138: [mvh] reference name Mire -> Mulgi (submitted by Jim Roberts, SIL Chad).
sources.note: Nothing. p.2: 'To date, there are no references in the linguistic literature to this language... work on the language is still at its beginnings.' Autonym Mulgi; 11-12 villages; est. 5-10,000 speakers.
